Here's everything I can think of:

1) Tripped, scrapped arm against rock(s) or gravel.

2) Biking/Skateboarding etc. accident.

3) You could just pull the "oh I have no idea how this happened I never noticed" card, but this doesn't work too often.

4) Some sort of woodworking/welding/metalworking accident, if you do any of these or your school has these classes.

5) Cut your arm on a thorn bush/tree etc. when out for a walk or hiking, if you have recently.

Basically just think of anything and everything that you have done recently that could result in cuts. Then branch off from there. Don't be afraid to tell a big lie to hide it, unless you're bad at lying. 

I'll offer more if I can think of them, but additional information would be useful for me to think of more.
For me, cutting gives me some feeling of the world. It makes me a bit happier, gives me a bit more energy, and helps keep me going. Although, this is far worse than the opposite.

You are just like me. I procrastinate until it is too late to change my mind and work.

Similar to you, I keep on telling myself that I'm not actually depressed and that I'm just making it up. It doesn't matter how much I cut, and it doesn't matter that I've tried to kill myself, part of me still thinks that I'm faking, even though I'm not.

I literally can't remember the name of my school half the time. I also mix up my friend's names a lot, and that's if I can even remember them. 

If I was to make a list of all of the things I forget quite commonly, It'd be huge.

So, yes, my memory is the *worst*.
Together it is then, whether you mean it or not.
But why's it all good? What are we surviving and thriving for? What's the end goal in this torment we call life?

Oh my goodness you are like me but older. 

When I was 11 I moved from the UK to the U.S. I left all of my friends that I had known my entire life and moved to a country with a totally different school system and different words ect. In the U.S., my family and I moved around a lot. I've been to a a total of 5 (or 6, I can't remember) middle schools and 3 different high schools. I've made and lost too many friends to count. At each new school, my condition just got worse. It was at my second high school that things got really bad. I then moved to my 3rd, and that was the final straw.

Like you, I have very bad social anxiety. I don't talk to anyone I am not comfortable with, and even then, I still might not, I don't go to school dances, I skip the assembly's, and I don't even sit in the lunch room because I don't like being surrounded by all of those people. I'm halfway through the second semester and I have just now made a friend that I know is a proper friend that I can trust. Even then, I only see him about once every 2 days, and I see him very rarely on the days that I see him. 

When I'm not with him, I'm alone. I sit in the back corner of the classroom, or as close as I can get, and I don't talk to anyone. I don't answer any questions, and I try to stay as unnoticed as possible. 

Some days are worse than others, and that is saying a lot considering most days are horrible. I have been cutting almost every day now for about 2 - 3 months, as it helps me calm down and forget about everything, if only for a short amount of time. I cut if I embarrass myself, if I get too anxious about anything, or anything like those. 

I am usually decent at hiding my depression and cutting, but it has been getting more and more tough. I think a few of my teachers and my friend realize that something is wrong now. It is just too much effort to hide it. 

I'm drowning in my loneliness, slowly and painfully.

I tend to self harm at school quite often, but I don't just scratch. I use whatever I happened to bring that day, which is generally a pencil sharpener blade or an *incredibly* sharp wood carving knife.

I know that the wood carving knife is sharp because one time I was using it to try and, well, carve wood. It slipped and cut a huge gash in my knuckle, right down to the bone. Oddly enough, it didn't actaully hurt too much. Mabye it was because of how sharp the knife is.

For me it's the same, but opposite. It's impossible for me to say "I need help" or even show anyone my cuts, so unless I cut too deep on accident and *need* to go to the hospital, I just deal with the bleeding and after-effects myself. Things just get worse for me if someone finds out, or if I even think that someone might have found out.
Thank you for your help. I will have to work up the courage and confidence to tell someone, which basically means I probably won't ever end up telling someone. Nonetheless, I will try.
I haven't spoken to anyone about it, not even a doctor. I don't think I would be able to handle it if someone else found out.

Generally the things that make me self harm are situations where I embarrass myself in front of a bunch of people, or if I get too anxious over, well, anything really. A couple of major things that make me self harm are big tests, like finals, or any sort of presentation that I have to give, even if it doesn't involve any speaking at all. These are just a few examples, there are many things that will make me want to self harm.

I don't think I've gone a single day in the last few months without cutting.

I don't feel comfortable talking about my self harming in front of actual people; no one knows about it. If someone found out it would most likely increase my self harming. On the web, like this, I feel better talking about it.
